cues: A phenol has its O H on the ring.
It is made by the Dow process, from a diazonium salt, or by alkali fusion, with a final acidification.
It is acidic because the phenoxide ion's charge spreads over the ring, so it dissolves in sodium hydroxide, though not in bicarbonate.
It couples to make azo dyes, gives phenolphthalein, aspirin by way of Kolbe's reaction, and salicylaldehyde by Reimer Tiemann.
Its activated ring is brominated and nitrated at two, four and six.
And neutral ferric chloride turns it violet.
text: Let us recap. A phenol has its O H on the ring. It is made by the Dow process, from a diazonium salt, or by alkali fusion, with a final acidification. It is acidic because the phenoxide ion's charge spreads over the ring, so it dissolves in sodium hydroxide, though not in bicarbonate. It couples to make azo dyes, gives phenolphthalein, aspirin by way of Kolbe's reaction, and salicylaldehyde by Reimer Tiemann. Its activated ring is brominated and nitrated at two, four and six. And neutral ferric chloride turns it violet.
